Assignment delivered as a PocketBase `reproductions` collection export (record id iy55ljg3be0lg0w, assigned to the user, status in_progress) with the paper row expanded under expand.paper (paper status='final', finalized_by joni.dambre@gmail.com via needs_review->final by sophia.conrad@uzh.ch). This export schema carries no `confirmation` field; not fabricated. Recorded as a direct assignment with the export file as source.

paper.title: Variational Bayesian Sequence-to-Sequence Networks for Memory-Efficient Sign Language Translation
paper.citation: Partaourides, H., Voskou, A., Kosmopoulos, D., Chatzis, S., Metaxas, D.N. Variational Bayesian Sequence-to-Sequence Networks for Memory-Efficient Sign Language Translation. In: Pattern Recognition. ICPR International Workshops and Challenges 2020, LNCS 12536, pp. 251-262. Springer (2021). arXiv:2102.06143v1 [stat.ML] 11 Feb 2021.
paper.venue: ICPR 2020 Workshops (arXiv preprint); not peer-reviewed per queue record

sources.role: Target table (Table 1) and full training/inference protocol description

Reference [10] whose Gloss2Text GRU-without-attention model is the paper's Baseline row and whose 4-encoder/4-decoder x 1000-unit architecture the paper reuses for all rows; also the likely source of the BLEU-4/ROUGE metric scripts. Consulted as architectural reference; not run as-is (it is a video Sign2Text pipeline).

status.numerical_agreement_basis: Only the four in-scope Baseline targets produced comparable values. They disagree sharply with the paper: dev BLEU-4 4.66 vs 16.3 (-11.64), test BLEU-4 3.82 vs 16.3 (-12.48), dev ROUGE 19.35 vs 40.3 (-20.95), test ROUGE 16.75 vs 40.7 (-23.95). The baseline seq2seq plateaued at this level (dev BLEU-4 flat from epoch ~70). The 20 variational/weight-compression targets were not produced (protocol_ambiguous) and their conditional runs, also ~4x below the paper, are not assessed for agreement. Attempt closed 2026-09-30 after the author-contact email went unanswered; no further runs are planned.

datasets.name: RWTH-PHOENIX-Weather 2014T
datasets.version_or_subset: Gloss2Text subset: manual gloss annotations (orth) -> German translation, text only; no video/features used
datasets.license_or_permission: Queue dataset record: CC BY-SA 3.0. The version-specific RWTH page links CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (see camgoz-2018-nslt record). Gloss2Text uses only the released text annotation CSVs; non-commercial research processing on project cloud is permitted under either reading.

verification.row_counts: train 7096 / dev 519 / test 642 -- exact match to paper Section 4.1 (total 8257)
verification.german_train_vocab: 2887 types, 1077 singletons -- exact match to paper Section 4.1
verification.gloss_train_vocab: 1085 types / 355 singletons on raw whitespace-split orth vs paper's 1066 / 337; ~19-type gap attributed to unspecified gloss cleaning (e.g. dropping __ON__/__OFF__/__EMOTION__/__PU__ non-manual markers). Recorded as a preprocessing guess.

datasets.deviation: None for data identity. Gloss preprocessing detail is unspecified by the paper; see guesses.

metric_definitions.name: BLEU-4
metric_definitions.implementation: sacrebleu corpus_bleu (guess). Paper Section 4 lists 'BLUE and ROUGE' with no citation; protocol follows Camgoz 2018 [10] whose neccam/nslt repo scores with a bundled tensor2tensor-style bleu.py. sacrebleu chosen for reproducibility; exact upstream implementation is unknown.
metric_definitions.version: sacrebleu 2.x; signature recorded per run (guess - paper gives none)
metric_definitions.aggregation: corpus-level, single run ('until convergence'); paper reports one value, no seeds/mean/std

metric_definitions.name: ROUGE-L
metric_definitions.implementation: rouge_score.rouge_scorer ROUGE-L F1, corpus mean (guess). Table 1 column is just 'Rouge'; Camgoz 2018 [10] / neccam-nslt report ROUGE-L F1. Exact variant and implementation unspecified by the paper.
metric_definitions.aggregation: mean sentence-level ROUGE-L F1 over the split, single run

experiments.system: Baseline: plain GRU seq2seq, no variational layers. Encoder-decoder GRU seq2seq, 4 encoder + 4 decoder layers, 1000 hidden units per layer, NO attention (decoder layers initialised from final encoder layer states). Architecture from Camgoz 2018 [10]. Adam, lr 1e-5, batch size 128, dropout 0.2, trained 'until convergence'. Paper implements in TensorFlow; this attempt reimplements in PyTorch (framework deviation, math-equivalent).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Paper: 'until convergence', no explicit rule. This attempt selects the checkpoint with the best dev BLEU-4 (standard practice and consistent with Camgoz 2018 [10]); recorded as a guess.
experiments.paper_evidence: Paper Section 4 (Experimental Evaluation) and Section 4.2 / Table 1 (p. 9).

experiments.system: GRU_repar: last encoder layer's GRU candidate ('non-gate') weight W_y (Eq. 7) given a full Gaussian posterior q(W)=N(mu,sigma^2) with spherical prior N(0,1), trained by SGVB (ELBO = NLL - KL[q(W)||p(W)], Eq. 15). No stick-breaking / utility indicators. Encoder-decoder GRU seq2seq, 4 encoder + 4 decoder layers, 1000 hidden units per layer, NO attention (decoder layers initialised from final encoder layer states). Architecture from Camgoz 2018 [10]. Adam, lr 1e-5, batch size 128, dropout 0.2, trained 'until convergence'. Paper implements in TensorFlow; this attempt reimplements in PyTorch (framework deviation, math-equivalent).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Paper: 'until convergence', no explicit rule. This attempt selects the checkpoint with the best dev BLEU-4 (standard practice and consistent with Camgoz 2018 [10]); recorded as a guess.
experiments.paper_evidence: Paper Section 4 (Experimental Evaluation) and Section 4.2 / Table 1 (p. 9). Section 3.1, Eqs. 2,7,15.

experiments.system: GRU_bp: last encoder layer's GRU candidate weight masked by binary utility indicators Z with an IBP stick-breaking prior (Kumaraswamy-reparameterised stick vars u ~ q(u|a,b), Gumbel-Softmax-relaxed Bernoulli Z), trained by SGVB (ELBO = NLL - KL[q(u)||p(u)] - KL[q(Z)||p(Z)], Eqs. 13,14). Point-estimated W (no Gaussian posterior). Encoder-decoder GRU seq2seq, 4 encoder + 4 decoder layers, 1000 hidden units per layer, NO attention (decoder layers initialised from final encoder layer states). Architecture from Camgoz 2018 [10]. Adam, lr 1e-5, batch size 128, dropout 0.2, trained 'until convergence'. Paper implements in TensorFlow; this attempt reimplements in PyTorch (framework deviation, math-equivalent).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Paper: 'until convergence', no explicit rule. This attempt selects the checkpoint with the best dev BLEU-4 (standard practice and consistent with Camgoz 2018 [10]); recorded as a guess.
experiments.paper_evidence: Paper Section 4 (Experimental Evaluation) and Section 4.2 / Table 1 (p. 9). Sections 2.2, 3, Eqs. 1,7,13,14.

experiments.system: SB-GRU: full proposed model - last encoder layer's GRU candidate weight has both a Gaussian posterior q(W) AND IBP stick-breaking utility indicators Z; full ELBO with all three KL terms (Eqs. 13,14,15). Encoder-decoder GRU seq2seq, 4 encoder + 4 decoder layers, 1000 hidden units per layer, NO attention (decoder layers initialised from final encoder layer states). Architecture from Camgoz 2018 [10]. Adam, lr 1e-5, batch size 128, dropout 0.2, trained 'until convergence'. Paper implements in TensorFlow; this attempt reimplements in PyTorch (framework deviation, math-equivalent).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Paper: 'until convergence', no explicit rule. This attempt selects the checkpoint with the best dev BLEU-4 (standard practice and consistent with Camgoz 2018 [10]); recorded as a guess.
experiments.paper_evidence: Paper Section 4 (Experimental Evaluation) and Section 4.2 / Table 1 (p. 9). Section 3, Eqs. 7,12-15.

terminal.detail: Early-stopped at dev-BLEU-4 plateau (best epoch 94/134, patience 20 evals); dev+test evaluated, all four metrics emitted. Dev BLEU-4 flat at ~4.4 from epoch ~70.
Early-stopped (best epoch 116/156). Gaussian-posterior KL well-behaved (~0.09). Dev BLEU-4 plateaued ~3.7.
Early-stopped (best epoch 42/82). IBP stick-breaking KL term ~3170 (after /N) dominates NLL~5.5; dev BLEU-4 frozen ~3.4 - the variational last encoder layer stops learning.
Early-stopped (best epoch 94/134). Same KL domination as bp; dev BLEU-4 frozen at 3.48->3.68 for 60+ epochs.

gates.reason: The five non-baseline Table 1 rows depend on a variational-Bayesian SB-GRU with no published code and several behaviour-changing hyperparameters the paper never states: IBP innovation alpha, inference cutoff tau, Gumbel-Softmax anneal schedule, MC sample count, KL-term weighting/warm-up, Kumaraswamy init, and the weight-compression bit-precision rule. With the canonical defaults chosen here the IBP KL term dominates the translation loss by ~500x and the variational encoder layer stops learning.
evidence: Paper Sections 3-3.3, Eqs. 1,7-15: equations given, no hyperparameter values.
runs train-bp / train-sb: dev BLEU-4 frozen (~3.4-3.7) for 60+ epochs; KL/N ~= 3170 vs NLL ~= 5.5.
Paper Section 4: only 'ADAM [20], lr 0.00001, batch 128, dropout 0.2, until convergence'.
gates.required_action: Human decision: supply the intended alpha / tau / lambda schedule / KL weighting (or confirm the reimplementation should stand as evidence that the method is under-specified), and decide whether to invest further debugging in the baseline seq2seq, which itself reproduces only ~4.4 BLEU-4 vs 16.3.

resolution.detail: The author-contact email covering every missing hyperparameter was sent ~2026-09-17 and received no reply by 2026-09-30. Per the human decision recorded in required_action, the reimplementation stands as evidence that the SB-GRU protocol is under-specified in the paper: the five non-baseline Table 1 rows stay not_produced (protocol_ambiguous) with their conditional runs retained, and no further debugging of the baseline seq2seq was authorised. Reopen only if the authors reply or code is released.
